articles.title: Luke Littler edges Scottie Scheffler and Jannik Sinner as the 'most dominant sportsperson' - Love The Darts podcast
articles.summary: After Luke Littler's dominant World Matchplay victory, Laura Turner and Chris Murphy debate on the Love The Darts podcast whether 'The Nuke' is the most dominant sportsperson in the world right now
articles.body:
'The Nuke' stormed to victory in Blackpool, winning the competition for the second year in a row and seeing off final opponent Gerwyn Price 18-9.

Littler being in total control at a darts competition is nothing new. He's won every PDC major title in 2026 so far, and his World Matchplay performance has made it very difficult to argue he's not head and shoulders above his competitors.

His mind-blowing performances have sparked debate over where he ranks in the sporting world, leading Sky Sports' Love The Darts podcast pundits, former darts player Laura Turner and darts commentator Chris Murphy, to debate whether he is indeed the most dominant sportsperson in the world right now.

"It's a very difficult question, how do you measure dominance?" Murphy said. "Darts seems to have more majors than any other sport, if you're doing it on major titles, but then again if you just took the top four and made it fair, he wins what you might call the Grand Slam titles.

"He holds them all and he's on course to have a clean sweep of every title so of course he does. I think yes [he is the most dominant]."

Murphy then named two other sporting stars that come close to giving Littler a run for his money - tennis world No 1 Jannik Sinner and his golf equivalent, Scottie Scheffler - but concluded neither can touch him.

"Looking at other sports, we've mentioned tennis, Sinner maybe he's in the conversation," he said. "Scheffler in golf has been No 1 for a long time, but I don't think any of them get near Littler."

Turner agreed, pointing out how rare it is to have two English people dominating a sport in both the men's and women's editions at the same time.

"It's very hard to say no [he isn't the most dominant] isn't it," Turner said. "From a women's darts point of view actually I think [Women's World Matchplay winner] Beau Greaves is unbelievably dominant, she's just picked up the Matchplay in Blackpool. She won 17 out of the 24 titles available in that qualification process as well.

"She's been on a run of 114 consecutive wins, it took Fallon [Sherrock] at a 102 average just to stop that run. Beau is very dominant.

"In darts at the moment I personally think we're very lucky, I know Beau is on the Pro Tour as well. I can't think of another sport where at this moment in time, anyone that is dominating in the way they are."

Does Littler edge Taylor as darts' greatest?

While Turner and Murphy have been wowed by Littler this month, they believe the teenager still has a while to go until he can call himself darts' greatest ever.

Asked if he is the best darts player to ever do it, Murphy replied: "No, and this is where I think we need to zoom out a little bit. Potential to best the greatest? Possibly, but I don't think it's especially close yet to be honest.

"It's not criticism of his abilities and talents, it's just simple arithmetic I suppose. Phil Taylor's title tally, 16 world titles, spanning across four different generations of darts players, and he's had to reinvent himself for different games in different eras."

Taylor, who retired in 2018, holds the record for the most darts world titles. Littler, meanwhile, has two, winning the PDC World Darts Championship in 2025 and 2026 after bursting on the scene in 2024.

Laura agreed that Littler has a way to go yet to edge Taylor, adding: "All of us suffer from recency bias. There's a lot of people don't forget that never engaged in darts to the level they are before Luke Littler came onto the scene.

"Ultimately, Phil has played through different generations, I don't want to say mind games but you know you can get under people's skin a bit more.

"Ability wise, and all the accolades he has won over all those years, you have to say Phil is the greatest ever darts player we've had.

"Luke Littler perhaps one of the most dominant sports people at this time."

articles.title: Commonwealth Games: Tuvalu boxer wins country's first medal without winning a single fight
articles.summary: Tarona Taafaki has claimed the Pacific Ocean island's first ever medal at the Commonwealth Games; the 20-year-old took on India's Lovlina Borgohain in Glasgow on Friday night
articles.body:
The 20-year-old lost her semi-final bout, falling to defeat against India's Lovlina Borgohain on Friday night after judges unanimously scored every round against her - however Taafaki still picked up a medal.

She reached the semi-final via a bye, and with only five entrants in her category and Commonwealth Games rules ensuring each semi-finalist receive a bronze medal, the boxer instantly made history for her country.

Her coach and father Badi Taafaki told the Press Association: "For the people of Tuvalu, this medal means everything.

"We're one of the smallest nations in the world, so a medal like this is hugely significant. We have worked so hard to get here. For me as a coach, it's a stepping stone."

Tuvalu, a tiny island in the Pacific Ocean, is the fourth-smallest nation in the world.

"When I was growing up, boxing barely existed in Tuvalu," said Badi. "We didn't have gloves, so we were forced to fight bare-knuckle, and hit bags filled with sand."

Athletes even train on the island's airport runway, as it's the most stable stretch of land amid the effects of climate change.

"Yes, we train on the airport runway," Badi said. "When a plane comes in, everyone moves aside. As soon as it leaves, we go back on the tarmac, because there is nowhere else to train.

"If we can win medals, more people around the world will recognise Tuvalu and begin to understand the challenges we face because of climate change.

"It is very real for us. The coastal erosion is unbelievable, and the countdown is now measured in years, not decades.

"Some islands have lost half their land. At high tide the sea comes right through. People living on the coast can't sleep if there's a storm, because the waves can come straight through their homes."

Taafaki is not the first boxer to win a Commonwealth Games medal without winning a fight.

Australia's Taylah Robertson won bronze in the women's flyweight category in 2018 despite losing her bout to England's Lisa Whiteside.

Taafaki's opponent Borgohain will now face Emma-Sue Greentree of Australia in the final.

articles.title: Commonwealth Games - Australia 68-50 England: Roses suffer comprehensive defeat to Diamonds in netball bronze-medal match
articles.summary: Australia inflict comprehensive 68-50 defeat on England in the Commonwealth Games bronze-medal match; England leave the Games without a medal as Australia make it seven straight Commonwealth Games campaigns with a medal; New Zealand beat Jamaica in gold-medal match
articles.body:
The Vitality Roses never really got going against a team who had already handed them a damaging defeat in the pool stage of the tournament, and a 19-10 Diamonds lead at the end of the first quarter proved to be unassailable for Anna Stembridge's side.

Australia, on the other hand, regain some pride by winning the bronze after their 46-45 defeat to Jamaica in their semi-final, meaning they extend their record of winning a medal in netball at each of the seven Commonwealth Games since the sport was introduced in 1998.

Jamaica have taken home silver, with New Zealand finally reigning supreme with a 56-48 win in the gold-medal contest.

"It was just so tough," England captain Fran Williams told TNT Sport . "When you come off the back with such a short turnaround to play in a game where you would be rather playing [the gold-medal match] later on is really hard.

"I was really proud of the way we showed up at the start and we just showed we weren't able to hold onto that with how the score blew out.

"We are gutted with that. Really disappointed."

The Roses - who arguably exceeded expectations after a turbulent build-up to the tournament including the departure of their head coach Jess Thirlby in March - got off to a fast start, managing to tie 9-9 with Australia in the first quarter, but the Roses scored just two more goals for the Diamonds' next 10 as the reigning Commonwealth champions started to establish a lead.

A 35-24 half-time deficit left England with a chance of getting back into the game, but Sophie Garbin's hat-trick for Australia towards the end of the period left a hefty lead of 13 for Stembridge's side to overturn, and a deflating fourth-quarter from England allowed the Diamonds to extend their lead to 18 and secure the bronze.

"Yesterday was a really tough day for the whole group," Australia captain Liz Watson told TNT Sports . "The way we came out and responded and have a really good performance and make a statement.

"We're disappointed about how we finished up with the bronze but we know how hard international netball is at the moment.

"We love to put on this dress, we have such a rich history of success with the Diamonds and we pride ourselves on doing that and wanting to be better."

articles.title: Raymond van Barneveld fined and suspended over inappropriate behaviour and offensive language in latest Darts Regulation Authority case list
articles.summary: Dutch darts legend Raymond van Barneveld, Cameron Menzies and Dom Taylor are among the high-profile players named in the latest Darts Regulation Authority (DRA) case list, published for the first time since 2022
articles.body:
The DRA, which is the independent body responsible for regulating the sport, particularly in events run under the umbrella of the PDC, WDF, Modus and ADC, has published an updated case list for the first time since 2022, listing all backdated hearings from January 2023 to June 2026, relating to various incidents that had occurred in both televised and non-televised competition.

Former world champions Rob Cross, Gary Anderson, Luke Humphries and Van Barneveld all feature in the case list, along with Cameron Menzies and Dom Taylor.

Van Barneveld, widely regarded as one of the sport's greatest-ever players, features in two separate incidents.

The first involves 'Inappropriate behaviour and using offensive language' at Players Championship 2 event in Wigan last year, resulting in a three-month suspension [suspended for 12 months] and £3,000 fine.

The second relates to 'failing to report damage caused to hotel room' following a Players Championship event in Germany, which resulted in a formal warning.

'Barney' is a five-time world champion having won the BDO tournament at Lakeside in 1998, 1999, 2003 and 2005 before making the move to the PDC the following year.

The doyen of Dutch darts made his mark by winning the 2007 PDC World Championship with a legendary final against Phil 'The Power' Taylor.

Sky Sports have contacted the DRA regarding Van Barneveld's fines.

Menzies' sanction for his outburst at the World Championship in December has been revealed , with the Scot handed a four-month suspension, which ended last month, and receiving a £2,500 fine after he repeatedly punched the underside of the drinks' table on stage in frustration following his defeat to Charlie Manby.

The incident drew blood on his knuckles, which he then wiped on his face before walking off the stage.

Shortly after the incident, Menzies issued a statement apologising for his actions.

"First of all, I would like to apologise for what happened," said Menzies. "I am sorry that I reacted in the manner that I did.

"It's not an excuse, but I have had a lot of things on my mind recently and I suppose it all just became too much at the end.

"It has not been an easy time for me with my uncle Gary passing away recently. I saw him four days before he died and he gave a look which told he much he thought of me. He treated me like a son.

"Had I won the game against Charlie, my second match would have been on the day of Gary's funeral and that has not been lost on me in recent days.

"Let me say again, that's no excuse for what I did on the stage. It was the wrong thing to do and I don't want it to take anything away from Charlie. He played well and deserved his win.

"This is not how I would like people to view me. Yes I can get emotional at times, but not like that and that wasn't right."

Taylor's failed drugs test at the World Championship resulted in a six-month suspension until June 18 , as well as a £1,275 fine in costs and the forfeiture of his £25,000 in prize money.

Taylor tested positive for cocaine and cannabis with the offence being his second which incurred a mandatory six-month ban under DRA rules.

"Accordingly, and taking into account all of the available evidence, the committee were satisfied that Mr Taylor's ingestion of both cocaine and cannabis occurred out of competition and was not following the commencement of the World Championship on 11th December 2025," the DRA statement read.

"Following on from this finding, the committee has determined that as this is Mr Taylor's second offence, then under these rules, he must serve a six month ban in line with 10.9 (a) and 10.9 (b) of UKAD Anti-Doping Rules 2021".

Taylor also lost his Tour Card as a result of the offence.

He had previously served a one-month ban in 2025 after failing a drugs test at the Players Championship Finals in November 2024. The ban was reduced from an initial two years after he agreed to undergo a UKAD-approved three-month substance abuse treatment programme.

Prakash Jiwa and Andy Jenkins both received hefty bans and were each made to pay costs of over £17,000 after being found guilty of match-fixing in the Modus Super Series from 2022-2023.

articles.title: Super League: Wigan thrash Toulouse to move second as Huddersfield win third straight match with victory over Catalans
articles.summary: Wigan Warriors move second with a win over Toulouse as Huddersfield Giants secure victory over Catalans Dragons; Warrington thrash Bradford; Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live
articles.body:
The Giants raced into an 18-point lead inside the opening 15 minutes through Halsall's double and Fenton Rogers before further tries from Wrench, Sam Hewitt and Zane Dunford put them 36-0 up at half-time.

Catalans rallied in the second half despite the dismissal of loose forward Franck Maria for a high tackle, with Ben Condon scoring twice and further efforts from Leo Darrelatour and Charlie Staines, while Wrench also added his second as Giants claimed the spoils.

Halsall raced 80 metres for an early interception try and prop Rogers barged over for Giants' second before Halsall dived over in the corner to put the home side in control.

Centre Wrench followed up winger Lewis Jagger's break to go over, Hewitt dotted down Tuimoala Lolohea's kick and Dunford crashed over for the Giants' sixth first-half try, with George Flanagan nailing all six conversions.

Catalans responded early in the second half when second row Condon burst over for Toby Sexton to convert, but another converted long-range interception try by Wrench restored Huddersfield's 36-point lead.

Maria was then sent off for the visitors in the 62nd minute for a high tackle on George King and although Catalans went over through Condon's try and efforts from Darrelatour and Staines, they were only consolations.

The Giants remain bottom of the table, but their third straight Super League win came after a club announcement at half-time in which they outlined plans to groundshare with Dewsbury at Flair Stadium next season.

Wigan move second with win over Toulouse

Wigan moved up to second as they overcame some first-half resistance from Toulouse before running away with it after the interval in a 48-18 win.

Zach Eckersley and Liam Marshall scored in both halves in an eight-try win for the Warriors, with Harry Smith boasting a 100 per cent conversion rate from the kicking tee at the Brick Community Stadium.

But Wigan, who moved to within two points of league leaders Leeds, did not have things all their own way, with their French visitors drawing level at 18-18 shortly before half-time.

Toulouse opened the scoring through Paul Ulberg stepping off the flank for a try but Eckersley touched down following a cut-out pass from Bevan French, who powered his way over soon after to put Wigan ahead.

Marshall then dotted down as Wigan looked to be moving up a gear but Romeo Tropis and Cesar Rouge struck either side of the half hour, with Rouge converting both to drag Toulouse level.

Wigan, though, went in at the break with a six-point lead when Noah Hodkinson went over in the right corner and from there, the home side did not look back.

Hodkinson turned provider at the start of the second half, passing back inside for Eckersley's second, while Sam Eseh crashed his way through several defenders to go over underneath the posts.

Jai Field raced on to French's chip over the top before Marshall's acrobatic finish and Smith's conversion made it 30 unanswered points as Wigan sealed an emphatic win to leapfrog Wakefield in the table.

Warrington dismantle Bradford to keep pressure on league leaders

Warrington scored seven tries to thrash Bradford 42-4 and stay in the race for a top-two finish in the Betfred Super League.

The fourth-placed Wolves are six points behind leaders Leeds and four points off Wigan in second with a game in hand.

Matty Ashton (2), Albert Hopoate, Toby King, Joe Philbin, Jordy Crowther and Ewan Irwin went over as second-from-bottom Bradford had their winless streak extended to nine games.

The 18-year-old Irwin converted every try and has now had 15 consecutive successful kicks at goals.

Despite Ethan Ryan striking an early blow for the Bulls with his 13th Super League try of the season, the result was never in doubt after Warrington established command halfway through the first period.

Ashton, Hopoate and King scored before the break and the flawless kicking of Irwin made it 18-4.

Bradford prop Jamie Gill had a try disallowed after Chris Atkin pulled back Danny Walker, further proof that it was not to be the Bulls' day.

Warrington did not take their foot off the gas as four more tries completed the rout, Irwin's the pick of the bunch after the teenager's twinkling footwork left the Bulls defence bemused.

articles.title: Tommy Makinson: Catalans Dragons wing and former St Helens try machine announces he will retire at end of 2026 campaign
articles.summary: Catalans Dragons wing Tommy Makinson announces he will retire at end of 2026 Super League season; Makinson turns 35 in October and won five Super League titles with St Helens during his career; Round 23 of Super League commences from Thursday August 13, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
The Catalans Dragons wing, 34, spent the majority of his career with St Helens between 2011 and 2024, winning five Super League titles in 2014, 2019, 2020, 2021 and 2022 and making more than 300 appearances.

Makinson also won a World Club Challenge, a Challenge Cup and four League Leaders' Shields with Saints, and was selected in the Super League Dream Team on three occasions.

A prolific try scorer, Makinson scored over 200 tries for St Helens and has since notched 20 tries in 37 appearances for Catalans after joining the club ahead of the 2025 season. He also represented England over 20 times.

"As the 2026 season moves towards its final stages, I feel now is the right time to announce that this will be my final season as a professional rugby league player," Makinson posted on Instagram.

"Rugby league has been incredibly kind to me, and when I look back on the journey I've been on, I feel nothing but pride and gratitude. I've been very fortunate to live out a dream I had as a kid and represent some of the biggest clubs both in England and France and also the pinnacle which is representing my country.

"There have been so many highs, some difficult moments, incredible memories and friendships that will last a lifetime. I wouldn't have been able to experience any of it without the unbelievable support I've had from my family, friends, team-mates, coaches, staff, supporters and everyone who has played a part in my career. To each and every one of you, thank you.

"I've still got a few games left, and I want to enjoy every second of them. I'll be taking it all in, appreciating the moments and giving everything I have to finish this chapter of my career in the best possible way.

"It's hard to put into words what rugby league has given me, but I know how lucky I am to have lived this life and played the game I love for as long as I have."

articles.title: Gian van Veen asks for help ahead of New Zealand Darts Masters with bags stuck in Paris
articles.summary: Gian van Veen arrives in Auckland for New Zealand Darts Masters - but bags stuck in Europe; Dutchman asks Qatar Airways for help as he prepares for World Series event at the weekend; Van Veen has just leapfrogged Luke Humphries as world No 2
articles.body:
Van Veen, runner-up to Luke Littler in the 2026 World Darts Championship at Alexandra Palace, has already arrived in Auckland for the event - but his gear has not.

The Dutchman, who has just usurped Luke Humphries as world No 2, wrote on X, tagging Qatar Airways' support page: "I am already in Auckland, but our bags are still at Paris CDG… I will need them before this weekend's World Series tournament. Is there anyone who can help me get them here ASAP?"

Qatar Airways replied to Van Veen, apologising for the mishandled baggage and asking him to contact them directly for further assistance.

Van Veen, the winner of the European Championship in 2025 and a two-time World Youth champion, will be joined by Gerwyn Price, Stephen Bunting, James Wade, Jonny Clayton, Josh Rock, Ross Smith and Damon Heta in Auckland.

The local players involved include Simon Whitlock, Jonny Tata and Haupai Puha.

This is the fifth of six regular World Series events in 2026, with Michael van Gerwen (Bahrain Masters and Nordic Masters), Littler (Saudi Arabia Masters) and Humphries (US Masters) winning the first four between them.

The Australian Masters later this month is then followed by the World Series Finals in Amsterdam from September 17-20, an event won last year by Van Gerwen as he beat Littler 11-7 in the final.

articles.title: Super League: St Helens miss out on play-offs for first time after loss to Leigh Leopards, Hull KR beat Huddersfield Giants to seal top-six spot
articles.summary: St Helens have missed out on the Super League play-offs for the first time in the club's history; Leigh Leopards and Hull KR confirm their spots in the top six; Round 26 of Super League continues on Saturday September 5, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
That result, along with Hull KR's 36-6 victory over Huddersfield, confirmed the top six as Leeds Rhinos, Wigan Warriors, Warrington Wolves, the Leopards, and the Robins.

It means St Helens finish seventh, without the chance to compete for a spot at the Grand Final, in what marks their lowest ever ebb in Super League.

The unwanted history, the first time they have failed to reach top flight play-offs since the 1964/65 season, comes on the back of a torrid season which saw them sack head coach Paul Rowley after less than a year in charge.

Now, they will welcome Australia head coach Kevin Walters for 2027 as he looks to bring the once four-in-a-row champions back into trophy contention.

It was a happier scene over in East Hull as Willie Peters got to sign off what is potentially his last home game as head coach with the play-off sealing win before he heads to NRL new franchise PNG Chiefs in 2027.

Saints reach lowest moment as Leigh show play-off strength

The task on the night for St Helens at the Progress with Unity Stadium was simple: Win to keep your slim hopes of play-off rugby alive. Early on they had chances to do that, but through errors lost the momentum and with a light bench, that meant trouble.

Leigh then found a foothold in the contest and took it. A kick left acres of space for Josh Charnley to walk in for his try, signing his contract extension with the club in celebration.

Two minutes later, Innes Senior broke downfield and David Armstrong's pace was too much to stop, giving the home outfit a 12-0 lead in less than 15 minutes.

St Helens hit back as they have good territory through the scrum and Tristan Sailor sent a nice flick pass out for Jacob Douglas to dive over in the corner.

They then came up with a sensational team try as Sailor came out to the left and then sent it out to Harry Robertson on the right who dummied and broke through. His fullback was there in support to finish off the play and then add the conversion to bring the score to 12-10.

However, it took just three minutes for Leigh to reinstate their advantage. Senior ripped through the left edge once again and this time, Umyla Hanley went through a huge gap left as Matty Evans looked to be taken out by Adam Cook.

With the try confirmed and extras added, Leigh made sure to add one more blow just before the break as Cook kicked on a speculative pass from Edwin Ipape to score under the sticks then convert for a 24-10 lead at half-time.

Things went from bad to worse early in the second half as stalwart centre Percival was sent to the sin bin for a high shot, the Saints faithful sending off their man with applause after he announced he will retire as a legend of the club at the end of this season.

St Helens had just under two minutes remaining of being down a player but could not hold out as Ipape barrelled over from short range under the sticks. Cook converted again to put his side 30-10 ahead with a quarter remaining.

Poor defending from St Helens then allowed Hanley in for his second with three men trying to take him down, good hands leaving Saints' line in more than disarray. Jacob Alick-Wiencke added salt into the wound with less than 10 minutes on the clock, the home crowd singing 'Saints are falling apart again' as another conversion from cook went over to bring the score to 42-10.

With merely seconds left on the clock, and the rain pouring down, the party atmosphere went up a notch when Robbie Mulhern capped off a night to remember for the Leopards with a try on his 100th appearance. Over went the extra two points and with the 48-10 win, the Leigh Leopards celebrated as St Helens were left to ruminate on a night to forget.

Hull KR secure Super League play-offs in Willie Peters' final home match

Willie Peters bade an emotional farewell to Craven Park as defending Betfred Super League champions Hull KR confirmed their place in the play-offs with a sweeping 36-6 win over Huddersfield.

Rovers' 47-year-old head coach, who guided them to their historic treble last season then capped that with a World Club Challenge title, is departing at the end of the season to join the new PNG Hunters in Australia's NRL.

Results elsewhere confirmed that although Rovers have now guaranteed their place in the top six, they cannot receive a home tie in either of the two play-off rounds.

Fears their top-six slot could come down to a straight shoot-out at St Helens last week were brushed aside as first-half tries from Elliot Minchella, Arthur Mourgue and Jack Broadbent snapped the hosts' three-match losing streak.

In fact, despite still lacking the talismanic Mikey Lewis, who is due to return from suspension for the last game of the regular season next week, glimpses of last season's historic title winners resurfaced in an impressively one-sided affair.

Huddersfield have long since shrugged off their tag of top-flight pushovers and headed to east Hull on the back of an impressive run of five wins from their last six under Jim Lenihan.

Toulouse move up to eighth with win over Hull FC

Hull fell short of a second-half comeback and were forced to accept a 44-30 defeat to Toulouse in France.

Henry O'Kane contributed two tries and Cesar Rouge added one try, six conversions and two penalties to hand the hosts victory in their last home contest of the season.

Two Lewis Martin tries and another double from captain Aidan Sezer after the break ignited a Hull fightback, but was not enough after Toulouse responded with a pair of second-half tries of their own.

Hull take on Leeds Rhinos away next Friday in their final game of the regular Betfred Super League season.

O'Kane opened the scoring with a sixth-minute try and added his second on the other side of a 15th-minute try for team-mate Luke Polselli and a close-range James Roumanos try.

It was 30-0 at half-time after Paul Ulberg crossed the line after collecting Mathieu Jussaume's pass.

Martin and Sezer - who also contributed five conversions - finally secured Hull points on the board after the break, and Logan Moy closed the gap to make it 30-16 just before the hour.

Rouge responded eight minutes later, and an Olly Ashall-Bott try with six minutes remaining put the comeback out of reach.

articles.title: Super League: St Helens 'need a big clear out' as team's recruitment questioned after missing play-offs
articles.summary: St Helens missed out on Super League play-offs for the first time in the club's history after 48-10 defeat by Leigh Leopards; Round 26 of Super League continues on Saturday September 5, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
St Helens' standing at seventh on the Super League ladder for the 2026 season was confirmed on Friday night after they were thumped 48-10 by Leigh Leopards, while Hull KR's 36-6 win against Huddersfield confirmed the top six.

It was Saints' seventh defeat in their last 10 matches and second heavy loss in a row, having suffered a 28-point reverse to Leeds a week ago.

O'Carroll is due to be replaced by former Brisbane Broncos and Australia head coach Kevin Walters ahead of the 2027 season, and the experienced coach will hope to galvanise the Saints back to their best next season.

But eyebrows have been raised over the team's recruitment decisions this year, with the club also struggling with a big injury crisis. At one stage in July, 16 players were sidelined with injuries.

Paul Rowley stepped down as the Saints coach that same month. Saints had been six points behind league leaders Leeds Rhinos at the time, but had suffered a 46-0 demolition by Toulouse earlier in July - the first time the club have gone scoreless at home in a league match since 1980.

The Saints, who won four titles in a row between 2019 and 2022, have experienced a sudden slump, and questions are being raised over the club's recruitment.

"Nothing is given in sport," Jamie Jones-Buchanan said on Sky Sports .

"You certainly can't copy and paste from one generation to another because context is king. St Helens probably need a clear out.

"They have some exceptional young talents coming through, but they're arriving at the wrong time, not having the best of experiences.

"Older players there too, who have maybe stayed a bit too long. Contextually, there are some players playing out of position.

"Tristan Sailor and Jack Welsby were really good against Leigh Leopards, you see moments of genius within it. But it's where they are playing and how it all fits together. The jigsaw has just not been great for St Helens."

Over the off-season, St Helens added experienced Australian players Shane Wright, Jacob Host and David Klemmer, while Jackson Hastings and Joe Shorrocks also arrived.

Saints also signed Daniel Suluka-Fifita midway through the campaign, but have struggled to make more acquisitions due to salary cap constraints.

It came after players including Konrad Hurrell, Morgan Knowles, Moses Mbye and Joe Bennison, left over the off-season, while Kyle Feldt was released mid-season.

The club has announced one new signing for the 2027 season, with Solomona Faataape joining from Catalans.

Sky Sports pundit and St Helens legend Jon Wilkin believes they have not replaced like-for-like and have made "short-term" recruitment choices.

"I've said it a number of times but Saints' recruitment has been shocking," Wilkin said.

"It's been terrible. They've made convenient and short-term recruitment choices. They've not replaced like-for-like and they need to rethink their recruitment strategy.

"There's a lot of young guys who have gone out into Super League who aren't ready. I'm loving that, it is great for them and for their future.

"But the reason they're out there was because you had an old squad at the start of the year that wasn't durable enough to get through a year, and then you signed shoddy replacements for guys who moved on.

"That's why young guys are having to put a Saints shirt on and are getting flogged by Leigh.

"I'm buying the message that it's all positive: 'Hey, we've got a great youth system and some young lads are getting a chance.' But if you look at the underlying reason why they are getting a chance, that's the issue. It's the root cause of their problem, sloppy recruitment over a period of three or four years."

O'Carroll: Missing out on play-offs disappointing

Reflecting on his side's season, and missing out on a spot in the Play-Offs, O'Carroll admitted that learning from this adversity may help his team move forwards in the future.

"I've just mentioned it to the group - it's obviously really disappointing," O'Carroll said after Friday's match.

"It doesn't sit well with me that I've been a part of that, I won't shy away from it.

"This group has had a lot of success, consistent success, so to experience a bit of adversity is good in some respects.

"Moving on now, I feel the conversations with Eamon and Abi, they have absolute clarity in terms of what needs to be done and I've every confidence they'll do that.

"For Kevin Walters to come in, it's probably a great time to come in now and for the club to accelerate forward."

articles.title: Super League: Wigan Warriors storm to League Leaders' Shield success with win vs Catalans Dragons and remain on treble course
articles.summary: Harry Smith, Liam Marshall (two), Brad O'Neill, Liam Farrell, Austin Daniel, Jai Field, Zach Eckersley, Adam Keighran score as Wigan demolish Catalans to win League Leaders' Shield; Super League play-offs on September 18, live on Sky Sports, with Grand Final on October 3
articles.body:
Having clinched Challenge Cup glory in May at Wembley with victory over Hull KR, Wigan lifted their second piece of silverware on Friday via a dominant home win over the Dragons.

Warriors scored nine tries through Harry Smith, Liam Marshall (two), Brad O'Neill, the retiring Liam Farrell, Austin Daniel, Jai Field, Zach Eckersley and Adam Keighran. Keighran also added 14 points off the kicking tee.

The only other side capable of claiming top spot and the League Leaders' Shield had been Leeds Rhinos, and owing to their far greater points difference, a victory over Hull FC would have been enough had Wigan slipped up, but Peet's side ensured that was never likely to happen. In any case, Leeds fell to a shock 18-12 home defeat to Hull on Friday.

Wigan will now seek to finish their season by clinching a treble with Super League Grand Final success at Old Trafford on October 3, having suffered final defeat last season to Hull KR. They and Leeds will have next week off as the play-offs begin, before contesting respective semi-finals at home on September 25 and 26.

Keighran: We're going into the Play-Offs with plenty of momentum

Wigan Warriors' player of the match Adam Keighran told Sky Sports:

"It was good to finish like that. The scoreboard is nice but it's the way we went about it.

"We spoke about going into the Play-Offs with a bit of momentum and that was the perfect way to do it.

"We've still got things to fix up and that's what we'll talk about next week, but it's good to have that and still win games like we did today.

"It was a group decision [Liam Farrell's late conversion attempt]. Someone said it in the huddle. With the career that he has had, you want to give blokes like him opportunities to do that.

"It's such a credit to Faz, he's unbelievable, the leadership that he's got, he's such a genuine bloke and I'm glad we can get a result like this and he can go out and lift the shield."

Farrell: Winning League Leaders' Shield doesn't get recognition it deserves

Wigan Warriors' Liam Farrell to Sky Sports:

"It [League Leaders' Shield] doesn't get the recognition it deserves. We spoke about it early in pre-season as something you want to knock off.

"You are slowly chipping away at it throughout the year. We've got there and this is a great end to the year and to do it like we did it tonight is great.

"I don't know the answer to that [is tonight final game?]. It's just all been about getting back to being fit. I've ticked that box. I had the conversation with Matty Peet, I said: 'Look, I'm there if you need me'.

"I didn't know how long I was going to play, I asked him before kick-off and he said 50 minutes, I was expecting about 10.

"I wouldn't like to be picking a player of the year this season. There's been some great players and in championship teams you need a lot of good players and we've got a few of them.

"I was lucky enough to get over. Funny, I scored on my debut and then again on the final game of my career."

Peet: I never expected this coaching success

Wigan Warriors head coach Matt Peet told Sky Sports:

"I never expected to be at this stage of my coaching career with so much success. It's impossible to expect that.

"There was doubt, plenty of fear and day by day, week by week, I'm lucky enough to work with the people that I work with.

"My job is to try and keep it on the tracks."

Asked whether this would be Farrell's last game, Peet said:

"No. In one way it was a good chance to celebrate it, I was always going to put him in this, because he deserves that. But now I've got to pick the 17 that gets the job done.

"He's a good player to have. I have a lot of gratitude to my players, still feel like... not an imposter, but it is a privilege to be associated with the club and play my part.

"This trophy represents the club more than the others, you know the consistency."

Arthur blasts 'erratic, poor' Leeds following home defeat to Hull

Leeds Rhinos head coach Brad Arthur told Sky Sports:

"We were a bit erratic at times. Some of our skill with the ball was very poor.

"We created more than enough opportunities. More than enough field position. Our forwards did more than enough on our edges and we were poor on our edges with our execution.

"It's an individual thing. Our skill was poor. We created enough chances and had enough field position.

"We have two weeks, new competition. But we're not happy with our performances at home. Not good enough. This place needs to be a tough place to come and play."

articles.title: Super League: Huddersfield Giants thrash Castleford Tigers in Accu Stadium swansong
articles.summary: Huddersfield Giants put on a show for the fans, running over eight tries against Castleford Tigers, in an emotional farewell after 32 years at their home ground; watch the Super League play-offs from September 18, live on Sky Sports, with Grand Final on October 3
articles.body:
Taane Milne and Jacob Gagai both scored twice as the Giants cruised to victory, made all the more impressive by the first-half dismissal of Fenton Rogers for leading with the elbow.

But it meant more misery for the woeful visitors, who slipped below their opponents into 13th place after a dismal run of just one win in their last eight games.

Milne marked his final appearance for the Giants with the opening try, and although Liam Hood hit back for Castleford, three tries in 10 minutes from Tristan Powell, Connor Wrench and Gagai put Huddersfield firmly in control at 24-6 by half-time.

Even Rogers' dismissal just before the interval for his challenge on Tyler Dupree could not gift the under-par Tigers a route back into the contest.

They did raise a flicker of hope when Daejarn Asi jinked through a static Giants defence to score the first try after the restart, with Ben McNamara's second conversion edging them closer.

But a penalty from Tui Lolohea, who also kicked five conversions in his final game for the club, followed by further tries from Zac Woolford and Gagai's second, confirmed an impressive Giants victory.

It also marked the end of the Giants' long association with the Accu Stadium under its various names, with the RFL having ratified the club's move to Dewsbury Rams' 5,100-capacity Flair Stadium from next season.

articles.title: World Series of Darts Finals: Michael van Gerwen loses to Daryl Gurney as Luke Humphries, Gian van Veen progress in first round
articles.summary: Michael van Gerwen's World Series of Darts Finals title defence came to an end in the first round as he was beaten by Daryl Gurney in a deciding-leg thriller; Luke Humphries and Gian van Veen won their opening matches as Josh Rock defeated Stephen Bunting 6-5
articles.body:
Van Gerwen missed six match darts at 5-4 up before being taken to a deciding leg which Northern Ireland's Gurney controlled despite boos and whistles from the Amsterdam crowd.

It is just the second time Van Gerwen has lost his first match at the event as his difficult 2026 season continued.

"It was really hard work. I can't remember the last time I won on a major stage," said Gurney, who has largely struggled to perform on the big stage in recent years outside of the World Cup of Darts.

"I put my darts away twice because Michael had six [match] darts. In all honesty, I was very lucky to even go 5-5 and I had the throw I was like 'please I need trebles'."

Gurney earned a late call-up to the World Series of Darts Finals after visa issues caused Philippines players Alexis Toylo and Lourence Ilagan to withdraw.

Netherlands' Maik Kuivenhoven and Gurney were the highest-ranked players on the reserve list, so replaced the Philippines duo.

Gurney raced into a 3-0 lead as Van Gerwen did not even get a dart at double but the match swung quickly as the three-time world champion won the next five legs and looked on course for victory.

However, Gurney stopped the rot to make it 5-4 then capitalised on Van Gerwen's half a dozen missed match darts to break throw and held his nerve to book a spot in the second round against Ross Smith , who beat Kevin Doets 6-3 earlier.

Humphries battles through as Rock beats Bunting

Also on Thursday, Luke Humphries battled past Dutchman Jermaine Wattimena 6-4 in another dramatic contest.

The opening four legs were shared before Humphries broke with a spectacular 132 checkout (bullseye, bullseye, double 16).

However, at 5-3 up, Humphries missed eight match darts but managed to get over the line, after missing three more match darts in the next leg, to set up a meeting with Dirk van Duijvenbode in Saturday afternoon's second round. Van Duijvenbode had earlier fought back from 4-1 down to beat Sweden's Viktor Tingstrom 6-4.

Josh Rock also made a comeback to defeat Stephen Bunting 6-5 by winning the last three legs after the latter missed match darts.

Rock will play Ryan Searle , who cruised past Rob Cross 6-2, while Gian van Veen beat Chris Dobey 6-2 and Karel Sedlacek saw off Ben Robb 6-4 in the other matches.

On Friday, the first round will conclude with Luke Littler, Gerwyn Price, Jonny Clayton, James Wade and Nathan Aspinall among those in action.

Littler has won every major title this year and will look to continue his remarkable record by winning the World Series of Darts Finals for a second time.

articles.title: Wakefield Trinity reach Super League semi-finals for first time with 26-16 win over Leigh Leopards despite Emre Guler red card
articles.summary: Wakefield Trinity have made the Super League semi-finals for the first time in the club's history; The Super League Eliminators continue on Saturday October 19 as Warrington Wolves host Hull KR, with kick-off at 5.30pm live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Trinity were thrown a spanner in the works in the second half when Emre Guler was shown a red card for what appeared to be a punch in a tackle with Owen Trout, reducing the home team to 12 players.

However, Wakefield had done enough prior to that to see them over the line and continue their incredible rise since returning back to the top flight in 2024.

Wakefield had a narrow half-time lead thanks to a Max Jowitt penalty, plus tries from Tyson Smoothy and Tom Johnstone, with Jowitt converting one of the two for their 12 points.

Leigh hit back just before the half-time hooter through David Armstrong and a conversion from Adam Cook to bring the score to 12-6.

However, early in the second half, Wakefield took charge through their forward pack, with converted tries from Isaiah Vagan and Caius Faatili moving them way ahead.

Guler's card then halted their control and Leigh hit back through Lachlan Lam and, later on, Innes Senior.

Despite Leigh giving it their all, a Jowitt penalty kept the visitors at arm's length and secured their biggest win to date.

Wakefield will now wait to find out whether they will face Wigan Warriors or Leeds Rhinos in the semi-finals. Their opponent depends upon the winner of Warrington Wolves vs Hull KR, which is live on Sky Sports on Saturday 19 September, with kick-off at 5.30pm.

Wakefield make more history as forward pack impresses

On a maiden home play-off night at the DIY Kitchens Stadium, it was a full-throttle opening 15 minutes, both outfits going end-to-end as the Eliminators' intensity was on full show.

The only points that came in that opening quarter were from the boot of Jowitt for an early penalty on the fourth minute.

After kicking a beautiful 40/20 just a few sets earlier, Smoothy opened the try-scoring on the 18th minute on the back of a repeat set. The experienced No 9 barrelled over and outstretched the defenders, with Jowitt converting to open up an 8-0 lead.

The Wakefield faithful then got even louder 10 minutes later when Johnstone went over in the corner. The effort was sent up as a 'No Try' for the video referee but it was overruled, ensuring the hosts held a 12-0 advantage.

However, just on the stroke of half-time, Lam threw a silky double pump pass, and Armstrong was there in support to race away and score with 20 seconds left on the clock. Cook converted to put six points between the two sides but it was clear with 40 minutes to go, Leigh still had a job on their hands.

Wakefield's forward pack had been on top throughout the entire encounter prior to the break and it continued to pay dividends just five minutes into the second half when Vagana stormed through to score, with Jowitt converting for an 18-6 lead.

The heavens then opened in West Yorkshire but that did not stop the Wakefield pack rolling through. Faatili was the next to bulldoze over with half an hour still to play, and as Jowitt added the extras, they led 24-6.

Leigh thought they had hit back through Innes Senior, but Owen Trout had taken Walmsley out off the ball in the build-up, and so the effort was chalked off. Wakefield still led by three converted tries.

Despite such a positive night, Wakefield were put under pressure for the final 20 minutes after a head loss from Guler. He was shown a straight red for what appeared to be a punch to the face of Owen Trout, with the home team needing to defend their lead for 20 minutes with a player down.

Leigh breached the defence when Trout broke through, ending with Lam in support on the left to race away and score. With Cook's conversion, the score was 24-12 with 15 minutes remaining.

With the player advantage, Leigh looked the stronger team in attack but could not extend their lead and when they were pinged for a dangerous tackle on Jazz Tevaga, Jowitt slotted over the penalty to move Wakefield more than two scores in front once again.

That lead was once again dented when Senior went over in the corner, but it was too little too late.

Wakefield were through to a maiden semi-final with a 26-16 victory and Leigh were left thinking 'what if' once again.

Powell: We have an unbelievable pack | Lam: Our start to second half was diabolical

Wakefield head coach Daryl Powell to Sky Sports:

"Really pleased. It was a pretty eventful game.

"I thought we did some outstanding things, and at half-time should have been well ahead.

"The game didn't pan out like that, but the start of the second half was also outstanding.

"We've been stronger this year, we probably lose that game last year. An outstanding, committed effort.

"Unbelievable pack, we had to play with a man down, but the boys dug deep. Leigh are a talented team.

"I thought it was a pretty tough send-off, to be honest.

"We'll take what comes now [Wigan or Leeds], it doesn't matter what I think. We'll roll into next week and see how good we can be."

Leigh Leopards head coach Adrian Lam to Sky Sports:

"Not ideal. It was quite frustrating to watch at times.

"Too many mistakes, and everything we tried not to do. That's what happens.

"When you come to these grounds, you have to start well. And they've been good all year, Wakefield.

"But a couple of soft tries was exactly what we didn't need. The story of the night.

"We rallied, but the first five or seven minutes of the second half was diabolical.

"Everything we've not done this year has all come out tonight, for some reason.

"Down to execution and individuals in big moments. We beat them at our home ground in this game last year convincingly.

"It was a completely different story tonight."

articles.title: Wakefield Trinity make history: How inner sanctum's belief led to first ever Super League semi-final
articles.summary: Wakefield Trinity are through to the Super League semi-finals for the first time ever; The Super League Eliminators continue on Saturday October 19 as Warrington Wolves host Hull KR, with kick-off at 5.30pm live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
That inner sanctum, among others, consists of owner Matt Ellis, head of recruitment Ste Mills, and head coach Daryl Powell.

Working in tandem, they came up with a plan for how they would continually progress: they have signed raw talent, made them stars, provided a stadium that both home and away fans enjoy attending, and now brought the progressive and rapid success that their most faithful have been waiting so long to see.

An example of turning that raw talent into a shining diamond? Caleb Hamlin-Uele. Wakefield saw something in a player who was not breaking through in the NRL. They brought him into the Championship, moulded him, made him one of Super League's best props, and now he is truly in contention to represent England at the World Cup this autumn.

Of course, the biggest success of all would be a trophy. But for now, they are through to their first ever Super League semi-final after their 26-16 victory over Leigh in the Eliminators.

Wakefield's victory was down to their immense forward pack which took control early in the second half. Even with Emre Guler shown red on the hour mark for what appeared to be a punch, they had done enough to keep Leigh at arm's length and see the game home.

It is further reward for what has been a remarkable rise from Wakefield.

"We are going to go where we are going to go. We are just going to prepare as best we can," Powell said.

"Wakefield have never won a play-off game - that is a box ticked.

"Now it is whether we can win a Grand Final. We have two games to do something special.

"You are one game away from getting to a Grand Final that would be huge for the club.

"You have got to be excited by that. We are all excited about how good we can be as a team.

"We will do everything we need to in order to give ourselves the best chance to do that."

Powell has been there and done this before with a team that was not expected to be at the big dance. Castleford, back in 2017, blew everyone away, won the League Leaders' Shield, then beat St Helens with a Luke Gale drop goal to make it to Old Trafford.

They could not complete the final hurdle.

Wakefield have two more hurdles to go. A semi-final against either Wigan Warriors or Leeds Rhinos. A win in that? Then they go to the Theatre of Dreams trying to complete theirs.

If they do that, the inner sanctum's belief that raw potential can become greatness will have been achieved.

articles.title: Warrington 35-12 Hull KR: Matty Ashton hat-trick helps Wolves set up Super League semi-final vs Leeds as Peta Hiku sees red
articles.summary: Warrington into semis for the first time since 2024; loss brings an end to Willie Peters' reign; Peta Hiku was shown a red card for punch on George Williams; the Super League semi-finals take place on Friday September 25 and Saturday September 26, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
It marks Warrington's first semi-final since 2024 after they missed out on the play-offs in 2025.

It also means Willie Peters' tenure as Robins head coach is now over after his reign which featured the history-making season in 2025 in which he won the Super League for the club for the first time.

The flashpoint of the game came early in the second half when Peta Hiku saw red for a punch on George Williams and the player advantage for Warrington eventually became too much for Hull KR to contend with.

Warrington had a narrow 12-6 lead at half-time thanks to a converted Ben Currie try, Ewan Irwin penalty and Matty Ashton's score. Hull KR hit back through a Joe Burgess wonder-try that was started by Arthur Mourgue to get themselves in the game.

After Hiku's red card, Ashton scored twice more to complete his hat-trick with Albert Hopoate also crossing the whitewash.

Hull KR had gone over through Dean Hadley but it ended up merely a consolation at the full-time whistle, Williams rubbing salt in the wound with a late drop goal and Toby King finishing things off with a try.

Warrington will head to play Leeds on Friday September 25, with kick-off at 8pm live on Sky Sports as they compete for a spot in the Grand Final. Wigan Warriors will then host Wakefield Trinity on Saturday September 26, with kick-off at 5.30pm on Sky Sports , as they bid to complete the final two.

Warrington a step closer to Grand Final as Peters era comes to close

After an early repeat set, it was not long until some eyes-up rugby saw Warrington get the first points on the board. Williams had some incredible vision to send the grubber kick through and while Burgess collected it, he half fumbled, which allowed Currie to collect and go in under the sticks.

Irwin converted and the home team were quickly 6-0 up, much to the delight of a packed-out Halliwell Jones Stadium.

Ill-discipline was costing the Robins and, once again, Warrington turned that into points. Irwin slotted over the penalty for offside and an eight-point lead was in place within 15 minutes.

Tries were then denied for both sides in corner-flying finishes from Ashton and Burgess that looked sublime, but neither winger could get the ball down before being bulldozed into touch.

With four minutes left of the half, the Robins scored a sensational full-length effort started off by a pass from Jack Broadbent to Mourgue who used his step and raced 70 metres before finding Burgess who did the rest. Mourgue converted and there were just two points in it.

That closeness did not last for long, as on the stroke of half-time, Kelepi Tanginoa broke through and found Ashton who used his pace to dive in for his 100th Super League try. Irwin's conversion attempt hit the post, so Warrington walked in with a 12-6 lead after 40 minutes of enthralling rugby league.

The key moment of the game came three minutes into the second half when a suspected punch from Hiku on Williams resulted in a red card. There was not much force in it but he hit the Warrington captain's face and left the Robins with 12 for the remainder.

Warrington made sure to immediately capitalise from it as they sent it out wide for Ashton to finish off his second try. It looked to be a forward pass but was given and so the Wolves were 16-6 up with 35 minutes remaining.

Despite being a player down, Hull KR would not give up and got their reward in the 53rd minute when a breakaway from Burgess was eventually finished by Hadley barrelling over from close range. Mourgue converted to bring the score to 16-12 and we had a game on our hands.

The tension had reached a new level inside Warrington's home but it was alleviated with just a quarter to go. James Bentley came up with a massive interception and Ashton followed to pick up from the play the ball and race away for his hat-trick.

That felt like the crucial score and Warrington then took control as Hopoate went in with a brilliant dive at the corner and Irwin came through clutch for a 16-point lead.

Just to rub salt in the wound, Williams sent over the one-pointer and, with a minute on the clock, King walked through and Irwin wrapped up the 35-12 victory and a spot in the semi-finals.

In the away end, there was extended applause for outgoing head coach Peters and the dynasty he has built. Burgess, meanwhile, celebrated on the pitch with his family as he continues his quest to do something just as monumental for Warrington.

Peters: Discipline cost us | Burgess: We should have closed out game earlier

Hull KR head coach Willie Peters, speaking to Sky Sports:

"Discipline has cost us a lot this year, and unfortunately it did again tonight, but I can't fault the players. I'm really proud of them. They kept fighting until the end.

"Warrington played really well and have been a very good team all year. I wish them all the best, but I'm really, really proud of this group and what they've achieved over the last four years. We've made a lot of beautiful memories.

"When you're down to 12 men it makes things difficult, but we still put ourselves in the game. We scored at the other end, went two points ahead and then, against the run of play, they scored.

"Fatigue always creeps in and it did towards the back end of the game. Peta has been great for us for three years. What he did was probably the wrong thing, but he's been outstanding for me throughout that time."

Warrington Wolves head coach Sam Burgess, speaking to Sky Sports:

"I'm proud of the group. It was a strange game, but we're pleased to come through and get another week together, which is what we came for. In the first half we felt really dominant and were disappointed with the scoreline.

"We left two or three tries out there and probably a couple more in the second half. We've just got to understand how important precision is because, over the course of a game, those moments add up. We could have finished the game much earlier."

articles.title: Willie Peters era at Hull KR ends after eliminator loss: 'Thank you for the memories, I will miss you dearly'
articles.summary: Hull KR will not defend their Betfred Super League title at Old Trafford after losing to Warrington in the eliminators; It brings an end to Willie Peters' four-year reign at the Robins in which he helped them to a historic treble
articles.body:
That was thanks to the guidance of Willie Peters. In his third year in charge of the club, he helped them 'climb Everest' and make history.

Not only did they win the Betfred Super League, they picked up the League Leaders' Shield and Challenge Cup, and then topped that off with a World Club Challenge win over Brisbane Broncos.

Every trophy was theirs. They simply were the team to beat, but no one could.

It was announced part way through this season that 2026 would mark Peters' final season in charge of the Robins before he heads to pastures new to take charge of the NRL's newest franchise, the PNG Chiefs.

The task was set: Finish on a high for their leader. Unfortunately for those from east Hull, they did not get the fairytale ending to close out Peters' four years in charge as they went out in the eliminators to Warrington Wolves after finishing sixth in the table.

However, Peters views it as "the best four years of his life" of which he is immensely proud.

"Discipline has cost us a lot this year, and unfortunately tonight, but I can't fault them," Peters told Sky Sports after the defeat at Warrington.

"I am really proud of them. They kept fighting to the end. Warrington played really well and have been a very good team all year. I wish them all the best, but I'm really, really proud of the group and proud of what they've achieved over the last four years at the club. We've made a lot of beautiful memories.

"When you're down to 12 men it makes it difficult, but we put ourselves in the game. We scored down the other end, went two points ahead and then, against the run of play, they scored.

"Fatigue always creeps in and it did towards the back end of the game. Peta (Hiku) has been great for us for three years. What he did [get sent off] was probably the wrong thing, but he's been outstanding for me over the last three years.

"We've got a lot of great memories, that's for sure, but they're still here, still cheering for their team. We're a close-knit club. We're a club that wanted to win trophies, and we have, but the fight tonight shows what this place is about.

"We were well beaten, but we still showed a lot of fight. My family and I have had an absolute ball. We've loved it over here and we'll never forget our time at Hull KR.

"I do feel loved, absolutely. Love's important. I remember Russell Crowe saying years ago at South (Sydney Rabbitohs) that it's all about the love, and there's something in that.

"When you're part of a family and create the right environment, especially in sport, where everyone cares about each other, you can do wonderful things.

"There's no doubt I've felt the love from the fans and the players, and vice versa. I love them too. When there's genuine care and love for each other, you can achieve special things.

"I love it over here. I'm really looking forward to the next chapter and to having a positive impact on a country (Papua New Guinea) through rugby league, both on and off the field.

"It's similar to what we've done here, but on a bigger scale. I'm really excited about that challenge."

Peters to return to Super League one day? 'Never say never'

While this particular chapter is closed for Peters and he has ticked off his goal of coaching in Super League, he admits he will never close the book on the UK.

But for now, he is focused on achieving the next goal which is being a head coach in the NRL.

Despite that, he will continue to back the European competition and ensure it gets the "recognition it deserves".

"We have loved it here. This has been home, and probably this year was the first time it really felt like home, which made it even harder knowing I was leaving. My family and I have loved it, so you never say never," he added.

"I am proud. I've got a great support network and I've loved working with everyone. You've all been great. The rugby league community over here has been fantastic. The game is in a positive place and I think there's a lot of growth ahead in the next few years.

"The product is outstanding and it's finally getting the recognition it deserves, even in Australia.

"I don't think Super League has always received the respect it merits, but I've always respected it. That's why I played here and why I always wanted to coach here.

"I'm proud to have been involved in Super League as a coach, and now I've got some goals to tick off when I return to the NRL.

"Just thank you for the memories and thank you for the support they've given me. They've made me a better person and a better coach.

"I've now got an opportunity to return to the NRL, something I've always wanted to do, and it's purely because of what they've achieved.

"At the end of the day, the players decide how hard they want to work and where they want to get to, and they've been massive for me and my family.

"I also want to acknowledge the board, who have been incredibly supportive. Everyone at Hull KR, I'm going to miss dearly. Thank you to everyone, including the away fans. The support I've received has been incredible. So, thank you."

articles.title: World Series of Darts Finals: Luke Littler threatens Netherlands tournament boycott after being booed and whistled at by Amsterdam crowd
articles.summary: Luke 'The Nuke' Littler was booed and whistled at by fans in the Netherlands during his dramatic second-round victory over Nathan Aspinall; the world No 1 threatened a boycott of Dutch darts events, similar to what he has done in Germany as a result of his treatment from fans there
articles.body:
'The Nuke' moved a step closer to becoming the first man to win all 10 major televised tournaments in a calendar year, having triumphed in the first five, with a hard-fought win over Aspinall in Amsterdam.

Littler won the last two legs to prevail 10-9 but the match was overshadowed by the crowd's behaviour towards him.

The back-to-back world champion faced a hostile environment during Friday's win over home favourite Danny Noppert and it escalated on Saturday night as referee Charlie Costorphine had to intervene in the last-16 win over Aspinall.

Littler has taken a stance against volatile crowds before, refusing to travel to European Tour events in Germany as a result of his treatment from fans there.

And he is "100 per cent" prepared to do the same in the Netherlands.

"With the Germans, I haven't been for a long time, we will have to see in Dortmund whether it changes or stays the same," he told Online Darts .

"If the Dutch stay like this, then I'm not going to do any Euro tours over there. There's just no point in me travelling, wasting my time while I'm getting booed.

"I just want to play my darts, obviously sign autographs.

"The past two nights, I've done nothing, I've just walked off stage without thanking anybody. There's no point thanking everyone when they are booing me."

Earlier on Saturday, Gerwyn Price defeated Jim Long 10-5 and James Wade saw off Wessel Nijman 10-7.

Luke Humphries crashed out with 10-9 defeat to Dirk van Duijvenbode, in the afternoon session, while Josh Rock secured a 10-7 win over Ryan Searle and Ross Smith beat Daryl Gurney 10-5.

An emotional Van Duijvenbode, who was joined by young son Levi on stage after the match, said: "Having my kid here is the best thing in my life.

"I won this game because he was here. When you are playing against the world number two you are always nervous.

"When I looked up at him he made so happy every time. It made me so relaxed. In the end that is the reason I won it."

Gian van Veen prevailed 10-7 against Karel Sedlacek and now faces Van Duijvenbode in an all-Dutch quarter-final, while Jonny Clayton battled past Motomu Sakai 10-8 to set up his showdown with Littler.

The semi-finals and final will take place from 6pm on Sunday, following the quarter-finals in the afternoon.

articles.title: Leeds Rhinos Lachie Miller: Injured star has 'no doubt' team can make it to Super League Grand Final
articles.summary: Leeds Rhinos opted to move Ash Handley to fullback due to Lachie Miller's injury that sees him miss end of the season; Watch Leeds Rhinos take on Warrington Wolves for a spot in the Super League Grand Final, live on Sky Sports on Friday September 25, with kick-off at 8pm
articles.body:
The Rhinos ended the season with a drubbing from Wigan Warriors, that effectively saw the League Leaders' Shield slip from their grasp, and then backed it up with a poor showing against Hull FC in the final round of the season.

That meant Leeds finished the season with back-to-back losses and had to settle for second despite sitting in first for the majority of the season.

However, that still meant they have had a week off to regroup, recharge and refocus before they take on Warrington Wolves in the semi-finals, live on Sky Sports on Friday October 25, with kick-off at 8pm.

One conundrum that they will have hoped to have worked out fully by then is their new combinations now that their star fullback Lachie Miller has been ruled out of the remainder of the season following his hamstring injury in the match against Wigan.

Leeds Rhinos head coach Brad Arthur has opted to move in-form centre Handley into the last line of defence to mike up the trifecta alongside Brodie Croft and Jake Connor.

Miller has "no doubt" that his side will get firing once again and make it all the way to the big dance.

"I am alright, I had a couple days to myself," Miller said to Sky Sports .

"It is one of those things. It is a tough sport we play and everyone has been through it at some stage it just wasn't great timing.

"I have just got to move my focus to the team and what they need.

"The beauty of Ash (Handley) is he is just a class player. On the wing, he was one of the best wingers in the competition. He moved to centres and is one of the best centres. He will probably now be one of the best fullbacks if he stays there.

"I have no doubt. We have been really good all year at home except for the last couple.

"I have no doubt that the boys will turn up. They have to get up for one game, focus for one game, concentrate for one game, and I have no doubt that they can."

Handley: I just need to go out and execute

Handley will play at fullback for just the second time this season in the semi-final and while he is aware he has a challenge ahead, it is one he is embracing for the good of the team.

"It is a big change, obviously I have not played there for years," Handley told Sky Sports .

"I will take on the challenge. Brad (Arthur) thinks that this is what is going to be best for the group and I will never turn around and say I am not doing it.

"I had a lot of pressure on my shoulders when I moved from wing to centre.

"I will give it my best shot. He is pretty clear of what he expects from everybody in each position, I just need to go out and execute it."

articles.title: 'I thought I won the fight': Suchika Tariyal calls decision 'unfair' after losing Asian Games semifinal on weight rule
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: Indian fighter Suchika Tariyal settled for a bronze medal in the women's traditional 60kg Mixed Martial Arts (MMA) event at the Asian Games on Monday .
articles.body: Indian fighter Suchika Tariyal settled for a bronze medal in the women's traditional 60kg Mixed Martial Arts (MMA) event at the Asian Games on Monday after losing a dramatic semifinal to Singapore's Hui Hoon Teo on the basis of the lower-weight rule.The bout ended in a draw after India's appeal was accepted, but under the International Mixed Martial Arts Federation (IMMAF) rules, the winner was decided by the fighters' weight recorded during the morning weigh-in. Teo, who weighed 700 grams less than Suchika, advanced to the final.A tablet computer or hardcover book is roughly the equivalent of the difference in weight between the two fighters.The bronze medal is India's first-ever medal in MMA, which is making its Asian Games debut at the Aichi-Nagoya Games.The result left the 36-year-old Suchika in tears on the mat after the final decision was announced in Teo's favour.The bronze also took India's medal tally to six at the Games. Indian shooters have so far won four silver medals and one bronze.Hailing from Kiloi village in Haryana's Rohtak district, Suchika is the 2024 world champion in jiu-jitsu. She has also represented India in judo at the 2022 Commonwealth Games and in kurash at the 2022 Asian Games.After the bout, Suchika said she believed she had done enough to win."I am a little disappointed with the result of today's bout because I thought I won the fight. I am not able to agree with the result. I was saying that this is not fair," Suchika was quoted as saying by news agency PTI."This is not fair. Because if you look at a player, he or she gives 100 per cent everywhere. And if you feel that the decision is unfair, then it is my right (to express myself).""I won both my rounds very well because I took her down. She did not even take me down. Yes, there could have been two-three connecting punches. I also landed a connecting punch. And in the last minute, she was going back and forth. Then I was applying my kick. I was hitting her again and again.”Asian Games full coverage | Schedule | Medal TallyDespite her disappointment, Suchika said she was proud to become India's first Asian Games medallist in MMA."I have given my 100 per cent and worked hard to reach here. I am happy I have won a bronze medal for the country."The semifinal was initially awarded to Teo. India then challenged the result by seeking arbitration.MMA Sports Federation president Nikhil Kunder explained how the decision changed after the appeal."We challenged the decision by paying an arbitration fee of USD 1000. Three new judges were added (to the earlier three) to conduct the arbitration and scored the bout again. When those three new judges came, the bout was scored a draw," Kunder told news PTI.He said Singapore then had two options under IMMAF rules."The Singapore team had an option to either counter-arbitrate where three more judges would come in and score the bout again or go for the weight that was taken in the morning weigh-ins. That's the rule of IMMAF (International Mixed Martial Arts Federation)."Kunder said Suchika weighed around 59.2kg during the morning weigh-in, while Teo weighed 58.5kg, which gave the Singaporean the win after the bout was declared a draw.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
