articles.title: 'Indian market is developing rapidly, we want to grow together': EMW Global sign cricketer Rinku Singh
articles.summary: Off the field News: New Delhi: For an athlete whose rise has been built on performances rather than publicity, Rinku Singh is now taking a big step towards building a glo.
articles.body: New Delhi: For an athlete whose rise has been built on performances rather than publicity, Rinku Singh is now taking a big step towards building a global brand. The India cricketer has signed with EMW Global for international talent representation, becoming the agency's first Indian client as it expands into one of the world's fastest-growing sports markets.Founded by Michael Rocha Keys, EMW Global has established its presence across emerging markets with a vision of helping talent grow internationally while connecting brands with local audiences.In a conversation with select media, Keys explained why India is central to the agency's next phase, what made Rinku stand out beyond his cricketing credentials, and how the partnership aims to develop his commercial profile through long-term brand partnerships and cross-sport collaborations in key international markets.Q. Why do you think India is such a special market, and what is its potential?Michael: Apart from India being an incredible country, with an incredible culture, and a love and a passion for sports, it's also a country which is quite close to my heart. The diaspora of Indians around the world is especially present here in London. Quite apart from my passion for the food and the people.Having made many visits more recently for my best friend's wedding, I do believe that as a market, they have been growing and developing and internationalising, and I think now is the perfect time for EMW to come into the market and to be able to get a foothold.Firstly, with one of the local stars of the sport, and then gradually, slowly but surely helping Rinku to grow his international brand, but also helping to bring lots of international opportunities from different diverse sports into the Indian market.The fans are amazing. We saw around the World Cup all of the different fan groups supporting many different national teams, whether they be Argentina or Brazil, and you can just see the growth of the market. It's exponential.You can see that also by the fact that the Brazilian national team are due to play against India very soon in a football match in India.The market is developing rapidly, we want to be involved, we want to add value, we want to grow together with that upwards trend, and we're very excited by that.Q. Rinku Singh joins an impressive stable of other star athletes like Olivier Giroud and Peter Cech. What attracted you to him?Michael: First and foremost, he's a character. I think we want to work with people that not just are sports stars, but also, in their own right, characters. They have an appetite for international growth, success both on the pitch and off the pitch, and I think Rinku embodies all of those aspects and those passions.For us, it's a pleasure to work together with him and to grow together with him, because athletes come in all different shapes and sizes.The most important thing is to have success in one's respective sport, but then to be able to build that success off the pitch, or off the court, or off the field into one's respective passions is definitely a match made in heaven for us, and it will really help us to grow and build his international brand.The market is developing rapidly. We want to be involved, we want to add value, we want to grow together.Q. Are there any other Indian athletes that EMW is looking to add to the roster?Michael: The short answer is yes. In the near to medium future, we will be looking at adding to the roster. However, in the near future, we want to be focusing on Rinku as our first client in the market to be able to help to build and grow and show the market what we can do. First, the priority will be on Rinku, and then in the medium term, sometime probably in the second half of next year, we'll be looking to likely work with other athletes.At the moment, the immediate priority is our friend Rinku.Q. What does a successful partnership with Rinku look like over the next 3 to 5 years, both in terms of brand expansion and setting a precedent for other Indian athletes?Michael: Success can be viewed in many different ways, but if you were to look at success from two main perspectives, one being commercially, from brand partnerships, and the other being from growth of Rinku's brand in international and other priority markets.As an agency, we're going to be looking to help him develop across both those spaces. Building out his brand partnerships, not just in India, but in other key markets, in long-term, committed brands that he also has an interest in.And partnering with other athletes across different markets to help build his brand in those strategic regions, whether it be across media, whether it be across content, whether it be cross-collaborations, like we've been doing a lot here in the UK with David James.The idea will be to help build Rinku's brand through commercial brand partnerships, but also talent partnerships and content collaborations with other top-level athletes in key sports and key regions.Q. EMW Global has a strong legacy in global football and has worked with legends like Messi and Neymar. What was the first thought when you zeroed in on Rinku?Michael: Having sporting accolades and being a top-level athlete in one's respective sport will only take you so far. I think one needs to have a mindset out of sports to be able to want to grow one's brand into the international markets, into other industries outside of sport.Rinku's openness and his passion to build his brand outside of India and outside of just the cricket space is definitely what attracted us to want to work with him on an international basis.Q. How can this partnership help Rinku's global profile?Michael: We are positioning ourselves as the world's local agency, specialising in emerging markets. We have offices across Asia, in Latin America, in Europe, and we'll also soon be expanding offices into South Africa, as well as the US in the coming years.The most important thing to help build Rinku's brand, which will be a process, is understanding his passions outside of cricket, and how we can tap into the diaspora of fans around the world who follow him in the emerging and established markets through partnerships with talent from different sports, whether it be basketball, football or baseball.There are so many different collaboration opportunities, and it's important to not forget that the world looks at India and sees the huge potential. Rinku provides that opportunity as a gateway for not just brands, but other athletes that want to build their brand locally, and at the same time can help Rinku build his brand globally.There really is an amazing crossover opportunity, both ways.Sporting accolades and being a top-level athlete will only take you so farQ. When it comes to expanding in India, will EMW consider non-cricket athletes as well? How do you build that in a market where non-cricket athletes don't necessarily command big money?Michael: I think that's more of a strategic question, and as we've just launched in the market, it's definitely a cause for consideration.Many international sports have come, some successfully, some not so successfully, and tried to launch within the Indian market. As we develop and grow in the market, we'll get an understanding of the challenges around that.Right now we're focused on launching and making sure that we can put the best possible plan in place for Rinku, both from a national and international perspective. Then we can start thinking about what the market holds in terms of other sports.Q. Your portfolio includes Giroud, Cech and now Rinku. They're great athletes but not always the biggest media personalities. How do you sell such athletes to brands?Michael: Everyone has a different personality. My personality is different, Rinku's personality is different. Everyone has a different personality and a different way of communicating. Just because people don't say a lot doesn't mean they don't have a lot to say.In front of the media, people have one personality, and in the dressing room, they have another.I don't think quantity is important. I think quality is important. Actions speak louder than words.When you have someone like Rinku, who might not have a lot of things to say in front of the media, I can assure you that when we're sat in meetings, planning projects and doing partnerships with brands, that is not the case.He's very proactive in the way he approaches partnerships, whether it's a brand partnership or an athlete partnership and crossover content, to make sure it's going to be very successful. articles.title: Rory McIlroy says how far a ‘good’ golfer should be able to hit their driver off the tee
articles.summary: Rory McIlroy is unquestionably the best driver of the golf ball on the planet. It is an absolute joy to watch McIlroy pound 330-yard missiles down the middle...
articles.body:
Rory McIlroy is unquestionably the best driver of the golf ball on the planet.

It is an absolute joy to watch McIlroy pound 330-yard missiles down the middle of the fairway week after week on the PGA and DP World Tours.

It's probably fair to say that we actually take the Northern Irishman's driving ability for granted now.

As we all know, us mere mortals cannot even dream of hitting our drivers like Rory McIlroy.

McIlroy has shared plenty of driving tips to help amateur golfers improve their games off the tee.

However, the truth of the matter is that 99.9% of golfers worldwide will never be able to hit the ball like Rory McIlroy, or anything close to it for that matter.

Rory McIlroy says how far a 'good' golfer should be able to hit their driver

The six-time major champion has suggested how far he believes amateurs should be looking to hit certain clubs through the air.

McIlroy spoke to Makeshift Golf and responded when asked how far a 'good' amateur golfer should be able to hit different clubs, starting with a driver.

" 250 yards, carry, " the six-time major champion said.

"9-iron? I'd say you should be able to hit a 9-iron 135 yards. "

When asked how far he hits his 9-iron, McIlroy said: " 165. "

" A 6-iron I would say 170 yards. I would say that's three clubs (difference between a 6-iron and a 9-iron) and you're sort of looking between 13 and 15 yards per club. "

McIlroy flies his driver up to 330 yards through the air, while he carries his 6-iron in excess of 200 yards.

He is capable of achieving those remarkable distances because of the speed he generates (around 125 mph clubhead speed and 190 mph ball speed).

It's like a different world to the one that the average golfer operates in.

Average driver distances for amateur golfers ranging from 0 to 30+ handicaps

Interestingly, the average driving distance for amateur golfers in the 0-5 handicap range is 261 yards.

Mid-range handicappers (10-15) average 236 yards off the tee.

Meanwhile, higher-handicap golfers hit their drives around 204 yards off the tee on average.

It's important to note that these are not carry distances, so the carry yardages would be substantially shorter.

The average driving distance on the PGA Tour in 2026 was 306 yards.

Rory McIlroy was second in the driving distance standings, having averaged 330.1 yards off the tee in 2026.

For players at the very highest level of the game, distance is such a huge factor nowadays. However, for amateur golfers, especially mid-high handicappers, accuracy off the tee is by far the most important thing.

articles.title: Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney buy historic pub next to Wrexham’s stadium
articles.summary: The Turf pub has featured prominently in the ‘Welcome to Wrexham’ docuseries
articles.body:
Wrexham's celebrity co-owners have bought the historic pub situated adjacent to the Racecourse Ground, which features prominently in the award-winning series Welcome to Wrexham .

Fronted by Hollywood stars Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney, Wrexham's ownership described buying The Turf as a "continuation of the strategy to protect the future of the club and its interests by ring fencing key areas related to the life of the club."

Originally named the Turf Hotel, the pub holds historical importance as the site where Wrexham AFC was founded in 1864. The venue plays a central role in the TV docuseries, now in its fifth season, which has helped make Wrexham a popular club around the world.

According to a statement from the club, bringing the venue under unified ownership with the stadium and football club "allows for the preservation of the history and traditions of the historic public house that is inexorably linked to the Racecourse Ground and Wrexham AFC Football Club."

Reynolds and McElhenney have frequently been filmed inside The Turf alongside fellow actors such as Will Ferrell and Paul Rudd, while Prince William once went behind the bar to pour a pint.

Landlord Wayne Jones has become a celebrity in his own right through his frequent TV appearances, and Wrexham confirmed he will continue running The Turf on a day-to-day basis.

"I look forward to continue running The Turf," Jones said, "and bringing its unique mix of history, atmosphere and sometimes Hollywood stardust to the next generation of Wrexham fans and locals alike."

Wrexham head into the international break in 14th place in the Championship after collecting 10 points from their opening eight matches. They recovered from a 6-0 thrashing at the hands of West Ham to beat Southampton 2-1 on Saturday.

The victory came after Reynold and McElhenney poked fun at the Saints prior to the game by using a playful social media video to reference last season's 'Spygate' controversy.

Southampton were expelled from the play-off final and docked four points when an intern was caught watching semi-final opponents Middlesbrough during a training session.

In a video released on Wrexham's X account, Reynolds appears from behind a tree, mimicking photographs that were published of the Southampton spy.

Promoting shirt sponsor Firefox, the Deadpool actor opens the clip by saying: "Today, for no particular reason, we want to talk about the importance of privacy."

McElhenney, creator of It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia, then adds: "Specifically, how to prevent spies from seeing what you're doing."

Reflecting on internet safety, Reynolds jokes about searching online for 'how to run a football club'. The co-owners then emphasize that privacy is "important to people everywhere", pointedly bringing up Middlesbrough, Oxford and Ipswich.

Reynolds wraps up the skit by saying: "Refreshing, huh? An organisation that actually respects your privacy."

articles.title: Steichen details reasoning behind red zone play calls in Colts loss
articles.summary: After the Colts loss to the Chiefs, Shane Steichen detailed the reasoning behind his red zone play calls in overtime.
articles.body:
With the opportunity to defeat the Chiefs in overtime, the Indianapolis Colts' red zone possession was stalled after the first two plays.

A deep ball to Laquon Treadwell and a call that could have gone either way but fell in the Colts ' favor set Indianapolis up at the Chiefs' 17-yard line.

Wanting to put the ball in Jonathan Taylor 's hands, Steichen called a run play on first down that went for a loss of a yard. Now facing a 2nd-and-11, Steichen again called a run play. This one went for a loss of two yards.

Just like that, the Colts went from being in an advantageous situation to facing a 3rd-and-13.

Steichen wanted to put the ball into the hands of his best playmaker, but the Chiefs were obviously prepared for that.

"I was trying to finish the game with [Taylor] with the ball in his hands," Steichen said afterward, via ESPN .

After a five-yard run by Daniel Jones , it was 4th-and-8 from the Chiefs' 15-yard line. The Colts approached the line of scrimmage like they were going for it, but ended up taking a delay-of-game penalty.

Had the Chiefs given the Colts a certain look, the plan was to let it rip.

"If you love it, man, let's go at it. Let's go win this thing. But if it's not the right look … let's kick the field goal here," Steichen said.

Playing for the tie and giving Patrick Mahomes the ball with a few minutes left isn't often going to be a recipe for success. That said, going for it on fourth down just for the sake of doing so, even if it's a bad look, isn't the right play either.

On paper, Steichen's reasoning makes sense, but the results did not follow, and the game ended in another Colts' loss.

articles.title: Ex-Blues winger Graham in hospital after serious accident
articles.summary: Former Birmingham winger Jordan Graham is in hospital after being involved in a "serious road traffic accident".
articles.body:
Former Birmingham City winger Jordan Graham is in hospital after being involved in a "serious road traffic accident".

A statement issued by the Professional Footballers' Association (PFA), on behalf of Graham's family, said the 31-year-old was "receiving specialist treatment" after the incident earlier this month.

Graham played 49 times in the Championship for Birmingham between 2021 and 2023 after joining from Gillingham.

An Aston Villa academy product, he also played 17 times for Wolves and had loan spells with Ipswich Town, Bradford City, Oxford United and Fulham.

In total, he has made 188 career appearances but has not played since leaving Leyton Orient in 2025.

"His family are incredibly grateful for the care he is receiving," the PFA statement added.

"They respectfully ask for privacy and that people refrain from contacting them directly while they focus entirely on Jordan and his recovery.

"Further information will only be provided when appropriate."

A statement from Gillingham said: "Everyone at the club is thinking of Jordan and his family at this time.

"We wish him a full and swift recovery."

articles.title: Longest-tenured Patriots player suffers ‘heartbreaking’ injury in win over Steelers
articles.summary: The Patriots got the win, but it came at a steep cost, as the veteran could face a lengthy absence.
articles.body:
New England Patriots starting right guard Mike Onwenu reportedly suffered a broken ankle in Sunday's win over the Pittsburgh Steelers .

Onwenu, a seven-year veteran, was carted off the field in the first quarter of New England's 20-3 win. According to ESPN's Mike Reiss, initial X-rays revealed a broken right ankle.

"It is heartbreaking when you see a guy like Mike, who has played through injuries, been here since he was a rookie," quarterback Drake Maye said of Onwenu's injury. "He leaves it all out there."

Onwenu's injury came after Steelers star T.J. Watt fell on his legs during a play in which Maye was sacked. Veteran Greg Van Roten replaced him on the offensive line.

The Patriots drafted Onwenu, 28, in the sixth round of the 2020 NFL Draft.

He is currently the longest-tenured player on New England's roster.
